claims.text: Mechanical alloying introduces high oxygen content into refractory high-entropy alloy powders.
Oxygen introduced during processing can produce TiO precipitates in NbMoTaWVTi.
Fine TiO precipitates impede dislocation motion, increase strength, and slightly reduce ductility in NbMoTaWVTi.
Using a controlled multistage decomposition profile under ultra-high vacuum below 10^-6 Pa will suppress both TiO and brittle alpha-HCP precipitation.
Heating at 300-400 °C will completely release hydrogen from the hydride precursors without causing sintering.
Sintering and extrusion at 1200-1300 °C under ultra-high vacuum will densify the alloy while retaining a metastable BCC matrix.
Rapid quenching or aging after extrusion will nucleate coherent metastable L2_1 precipitates instead of brittle intermetallic phases.
Either ultra-high vacuum below 10^-6 Pa or argon containing less than 1 ppm oxygen and nitrogen is sufficient for the proposed process.
Appropriate extrusion pressure can produce greater than 98% theoretical density without shear-induced cracking.
Metastable coherent L2_1 or related ordered BCC/B2 nanoprecipitates can act as dislocation-pinning sites without causing the brittleness associated with TiO or alpha-HCP phases.
A rapid thermal cycle can kinetically suppress stable brittle Laves or alpha-HCP phases in favor of metastable coherent precipitates.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces can permit dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations while maintaining precipitation strengthening.
The hydride precursor route avoids the oxygen uptake associated with mechanical alloying.
The hydride-extruded alloy will have a significantly lower ductile-to-brittle transition temperature than a mechanically alloyed and SPS-consolidated alloy.
Coherent precipitation strengthening will enhance yield strength at temperatures above 700 °C.
Preventing oxygen-induced embrittlement will eliminate catastrophic cracking during extrusion.
Mechanically alloyed NbMoTaWVTi powder can contain approximately 0.86 mass percent oxygen and form TiO during SPS.
Gas atomization can minimize initial interstitial contamination and provide hydride/refractory powders with less than 50 ppm oxygen.
Titanium is the primary oxygen getter in the proposed NbMoTaWVTi alloy.
Rapid hydrogen evolution during decomposition can cause porosity or microcracking unless extrusion pressure is precisely tuned.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator presents ordered BCC/B2-type precipitates as coherent and non-brittle, whereas the cited coherent-precipitation mechanism explicitly identifies traditional B2 secondary phases among phases associated with embrittlement. The hypothesis does not distinguish the proposed benign B2-like state from the brittle B2 state.
